image_description: A close-up portrait of a dark-furred sea lion resting on a wooden structure near water. The animal's head is turned slightly to the right, showcasing its wet, sleek fur, prominent whiskers, and visible external ear flap. The lighting highlights the texture of the fur and the moisture on the nose.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad with prominent sagittal crest in males.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head appears relatively smooth and rounded without the pronounced bony sagittal crest typical of mature male sea lions; likely a female or juvenile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: External ear pinnae (visible ear flaps) distinguish from true seals.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct, small external ear flap is clearly visible on the side of the head, confirming it is an otariid (sea lion/fur seal) and not a true seal.
Long, light-colored whiskers are clearly visible extending from the muzzle area.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Fur is short and coarse ranging from brown to dark grey, lighter on ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fur appears dark (black/dark brown) and sleek/wet, consistent with the description, though the 'coarse' texture is hard to verify due to wetness.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body exhibits streamlined fusiform form of substantial marine mammal proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and upper shoulders are visible; the full body shape is occluded by the frame and the wooden structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Males develop thick neck mane and are significantly larger than females.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is no visible thick neck mane, supporting the assessment that this is likely a female or juvenile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Foreflippers are large, broad, and hairless on underside used for terrestrial locomotion.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Foreflippers are not visible in this head-and-shoulders crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Hind flippers can rotate forward for walking on land.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Hind flippers are completely out of frame.
The visible portion of the head and neck shows natural biological symmetry without distortion.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The fur texture has a slightly repetitive, 'stamped' pattern in the mid-tones, lacking the random variation of individual hairs, which is a common subtle AI artifact in dense fur generation.
The wooden planks in the upper left show inconsistent perspective lines and slight warping where they meet the dark background, suggesting weak geometric grounding.
